forecaster_note: Fun sized peaky surf — maybe a brief AM window of SSW'lys, onshore SE wind PM. Mixed short period ESE swell plus some leftover S will give us some peaky surf in the chest to head range across most spots. A possible brief window of cleaner conditions around dawn from SSW'lys, and most likely to be lumpy across the exposures in the morning, still surfable, cleaner for shelter. Light to moderate onshores later. — Anthony Spinks, Surfline

wind.summary: Glassy at dawn — SSW offshore only 2/6 km/h until about 8am. ENE sea breeze fills in by 9am (3/8), swinging ESE onshore 9/13 by midday and SSE 11/14 by 3pm. The clean window is short and early.

shark.summary: SharkSmart NSW feeds are live and publishing again — 12 detections statewide in the last 24 hours (most recent: Maroubra Beach drone sighting, 16 Aug 2:16pm, followed by an all-clear). No detections anywhere between Palm Beach and Manly in the last 24 hours. The most recent Northern Beaches entry was a drone sighting at North Narrabeen on 15 Aug at 3:50pm, ~40 hours ago and well north of your four spots.

days.label: Today
days.note: Two swells stacked on each other: 3.8ft @ 7s from 101° (E/ESE) and 3.4ft @ 8s from 173° (dead S). The ESE one is the useful half — it swings straight into Dee Why and Curl Curl instead of having to bend around the headland. Energy is steady-to-building all day (102 kJ at 6am → 112 kJ by 3pm) but it is all short-period, so it's peaky and gutless rather than powerful. Wind is the story: SSW offshore at dawn (2 km/h, glassy), then ENE from about 9am and ESE onshore 9–13 km/h by midday. Tide drains off the 11:19am high. Best window is dawn to ~9:30am; the 10am–12pm slot is still surfable but getting lumpy.

dee-why.window: Dawn to 9:30am. SSW offshore holds until roughly 8am, ENE fills in by 9, ESE onshore 9–13 km/h from midday. Tide pushing to the 11:19am high — the Point prefers the drain off it, so a late-morning session works too if you can cop the bump.

tip.label: Frontside at the Point — pick the ESE sets
tip.text: 105 kJ reads healthy but it's split across a 7s ESE and an 8s dead-S. The 173° half is what makes Dee Why walls up and closes out; the 101° half is what makes the Point bowl. Sit wide on the Point, let the south slop roll through and go on the E/ESE sets — you'll feel the difference in the take-off. There's a 1.0ft @ 16s at 181° buried in there too; long period at that size won't build the wave but it will occasionally line up a longer wall. Get wet before 9:30am while it's still glassy.

alerts: 173° dead-S component wraps fat here — the 101° ESE is the workable one
ENE sea breeze from ~9am, ESE onshore by midday

long-reef.window: Dawn to 10am. Biggest of the four at 2–3ft chest-to-overhead. SSW offshore early, ENE onshore from 9am, then ESE 9–13 km/h at midday which is straight onto it.

tip.label: Size lives here today
tip.text: Same 105 kJ, but Long Reef converts both swell angles instead of just one — that's why it reads chest-to-overhead while Dee Why reads waist-to-chest. Downside: it's also the most exposed to the ESE onshore that arrives by midday. This is a dawn call. If you want the most wave-face today and you're up early, drive north.

alerts: ESE onshore hits this exposure hardest after midday

curl-curl.window: Dawn to 10am. Chest-to-head and peaky, tide filling to the 11:19am high. Best of the mid-morning options if you can't make dawn.

tip.label: Backside lefts, plenty of them
tip.text: Curl Curl takes the 101° ESE cleanly and holds size — chest-to-head on 105 kJ. It's a beachie on 7–8s spacing, so peaks shift constantly; walk the bank before you paddle rather than committing to the first channel you see. Your backside on the lefts here is the play, and the short period means quick, vertical sections — good for the FT, not for a step-up.

alerts: Peaky and shifty on the short period — banks matter more than usual

manly.window: Mid-morning is fine here. Smallest of the four at dawn (thigh-to-stomach) but builds to waist-to-chest by midday as the tide drains. Most sheltered from the ESE onshore.

tip.label: The 10am–12pm option
tip.text: Manly is the one spot that gets better, not worse, through your preferred 10am–12pm window: thigh-to-stomach at 9am, waist-to-chest by midday, and it's the least exposed to the ESE. If a sleep-in beats a dawn patrol today, this is where you go — just accept it's the smallest of the four.

alerts: Smallest at dawn — builds through the morning
Best wind shelter of the four after 10am

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Surfline flags Tuesday as a day to watch — 'fun sized peaky surf, clean to cleanish all day.' Energy actually climbs on today (110 kJ at 9am → 122 kJ at midday) and the wind goes light-variable rather than onshore: NE 3 km/h at dawn, ENE 6/11 at 9am, ENE 10/17 by midday but cross rather than straight onshore. Still all short-period, so peaky and consistent but lacking punch. Cleaner and more forgiving than today across the board.

dee-why.window: 9am–12pm. Cleaner than today with light ENE cross-shore, energy building to 122 kJ by midday. Smaller here than the neighbours — Dee Why is still getting the short end of the angle.

long-reef.window: 9am–12pm. Again the size magnet — chest to overhead on 110–122 kJ with ENE cross-shore rather than straight onshore. Best combination of size and clean water tomorrow.
alerts: Pick of the four for size + wind

curl-curl.window: 9am–12pm. Waist to chest, peaky and consistent, ENE cross-shore. Solid mid-morning option that suits the 10am–12pm slot.

manly.window: 10am–12pm. Builds through the morning like today — thigh-to-stomach early, waist-to-chest by midday.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Two very different days. SATURDAY is the write-off: energy collapses to 27 kJ at 9am and 16 kJ by midday, knee-to-thigh at most spots, and a 14/22 km/h WSW gets on it after 10am. SUNDAY is the session — energy recovers to 68 kJ, a 3.3ft @ 8s S swell at 180° with a 2.1ft @ 6s NE at 64° on top, and light W/WNW offshore all morning (5/7 km/h at 9am, 4/6 by midday). Values below are SUNDAY. If you only surf once this weekend, make it Sunday mid-morning.

dee-why.window: SUNDAY 9am–12pm. Light W/WNW offshore, 68 kJ. Saturday is knee-to-thigh on 16–27 kJ with a 22 km/h WSW — skip it.
alerts: Saturday: 0–1ft, 16–27 kJ, poor — not worth the drive
Sunday swell is 180° dead S again — Dee Why gets the fat version

long-reef.window: SUNDAY 9am–12pm. Best of the four again — waist to chest with clean W offshore. Saturday: thigh-to-waist and windblown.

curl-curl.window: SUNDAY 9am–12pm. Matches Long Reef for size with the same clean offshore. Saturday is the only spot still scraping a fair rating at 9am, but on 27 kJ it's knee-high nonsense.
alerts: Saturday marginal at best on 27 kJ

manly.window: SUNDAY 9am–12pm. Smallest of the four but clean. Saturday rates poor here — 0–1ft on 16 kJ.
alerts: Saturday: poor, 0–1ft — the worst of the four
